A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Graph-KV. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison; the original implementation appendix is retained and renumbered.

before.justification: v1 reports original RAG, ARXIV-QA, paper-classification, and synthetic scalability experiments in Section 4, with supporting appendix examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds backbone-applicability and multi-hop experiments in Appendix A.1, Tables 5-7.

M1.justification: Appendix A.1.2 adds concrete two- and three-stage RAG variants using retrieval-ranked chains and passing updated KV caches between stages. v1 already permitted iteration in principle, but its reported RAG constructions used one stage. The underlying attention and positional-encoding mechanisms remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same seven RAG benchmarks, ARXIV-QA, Cora, Pubmed, and synthetic star-graph scenarios. The added appendix experiments reuse six existing RAG datasets with different model and propagation configurations.

E2.justification: Tables 5-6 add Block-RAG to the 8B-SFT comparisons alongside PCW and APE. In v1, SFT comparisons contained sequential encoding, PCW, and APE, while Block-RAG appeared with 8B-Block. Existing main-text comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds Graph-KV evaluation with the standard 8B-SFT backbone and explicit two- and three-hop configurations. Existing experiments retain their preprocessing, ten-chunk RAG inputs, accuracy metric, output limits, and classification splits.

E4.justification: Appendix A.1 introduces systematic tests of two substantive questions: dependence on block-attention post-training and sensitivity to propagation depth. Tables 5-7 provide comparisons across six RAG datasets; v1 lacked corresponding quantitative Graph-KV backbone and multi-hop analyses.

E5.justification: The classification uncertainty entries and seeds 42-44 are retained, as is the ARXIV-QA distractor-seed discussion. The new checklist summarizes the existing three-seed practice; the added tables introduce no new uncertainty estimates or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 5-7 add results across six datasets for SFT-based Graph-KV and Block-RAG and for multi-hop variants. For example, SFT Graph-KV scores 15.47 on MorehopQA, while the new three-hop configuration scores 46.69. Original main-table results remain unchanged. Some duplicated entries disagree: PCW's 2Wiki inference score is 14.07 in Table 3 but 13.07 in new Table 5.

T1.justification: The graph definitions, attention expression, positional-range construction, and computational-complexity analysis are unchanged. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and the added experiments introduce none.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about structural bias, positional robustness, efficiency, and performance. The conclusion even retains its original one-hop-only evaluation statement despite the added multi-hop appendix.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 now explicitly qualifies Graph-KV's applicability without block-attention post-training: its advantage over parallel baselines persists, but absolute performance declines, attributed to distribution shift. Existing mechanism explanations and limitations otherwise remain, including the unreconciled one-hop-only statements.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1.2 specifies retrieval-rank groupings and update schedules for the new two- and three-hop experiments. The original implementation appendix moves from A.1 to A.2 with the same hardware, libraries, prompts, preprocessing instructions, model links, and code/data access information.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 73 works and retain the same related-work discussion and novelty positioning. Bibliographic reordering and citation renumbering do not change research positioning.

P1.justification: Most research prose remains unchanged. v2 adds a results-discussion paragraph, an additional-experiments appendix section, acknowledgements, and a NeurIPS checklist, with corresponding appendix and reference renumbering.

P2.justification: The document is reformatted throughout into a narrower NeurIPS layout, resizing and relocating existing displays. Tables 2-3 now share a page, and Figure 5 moves alongside Figure 6. Three new result tables are added; existing diagrams and plots retain their substantive content.

improvement.justification: Tables 5-7 provide useful evidence about backbone dependence and propagation depth that v1 did not substantiate quantitatively. This modestly strengthens empirical support, although coverage remains within existing datasets and the Llama-3.1-8B family. Unreconciled one-hop-only statements and inconsistent duplicated table entries limit the benefit.
